observation: Owner pinned Pace 4.1.5 at commit f510c134; the local checkout actually used was 4c5d2d20 on the same branch and every receipt reports version 4.0.3. Nothing in plan/apply warns that the installed kit is older than the requested pin.
expected: Installer surfaces or locks the requested version/SHA so feedback is bound to the intended release.

observation: First apply (27 items, deps added 88 packages incl. radix-ui and motion) was rolled back, then a reduced 'safe' 22-item plan was applied and verified. The rollback path cost a full plan/apply cycle and a 74-package uninstall. Likely trigger: plan contained LicenseRef-oxygen-owner-decision files (stat-card, table) that needed owner sign-off — inferred, not confirmed.
expected: Plan stage lists license-gated and optional items up front so the first apply is the final one; rollback is unnecessary.
resolution: Re-ran doctor→plan→apply→verify with the safe item set; verified:true.

observation: Pre-install research found the public site and the kit disagree: site advertises 44 components / 369 registry entries / check-usage, while kit/manifest.json has 21 file records, kit/registry.json 20 entries, and bin/pace.mjs has no check-usage command. DOM showed base-ui markers while the kit manifest names radix-ui.
expected: The published catalog and the installed kit are version-bound so a consumer knows exactly what the pin contains.

observation: The Pace token layer was retained wholesale: src/index.css line 4 imports ../styles/pace.css untouched, and the product's two successive brand themes (green Jana, then Crextio graphite/paper/solar) were layered on top entirely through app CSS. No kit file was edited to achieve the reskin.
expected: Brand reskin without forking kit sources.
resolution: Token foundation imported once; identity delivered by app themes.

observation: Owner rejected the straightforward green Jana recolor as not distinctive and supplied five Crextio-like reference screenshots; the whole app was re-themed. Adaptation happened in app CSS (crextio-layout.css, themes/jana.css), not through a Pace theme mechanism — because the kit exposes tokens to override but no documented 'brand preset' workflow for a direction this far from Pace defaults.
expected: A documented path for deep brand restyling: which tokens are semantic-safe to rebind, plus a recipe for palettes that are not 'calm neutral'.
resolution: Custom theme authored at app level over pace.css tokens.

observation: The safe apply installed 22 items; only 7 files remain on disk (card, cn, dialog, empty, native-select, skeleton, textarea + notices). Agents hand-deleted the other ~15 files (button, input, tabs, field, label, pagination, dropdown-menu, avatar, breadcrumb, progress, sheet, toast, separator, springs, motion-prefs, use-reduced-motion). Manual deletion leaves .pace receipts claiming files that no longer exist — a re-run of verify would now report drift.
expected: A supported prune/remove command that deletes unused kit files and updates the receipt, so verify stays truthful.

observation: The two highest-frequency controls (Button, Input) were re-vendored by hand into src/components/upstream/ from the Base UI + cva lineage (shadcn-LICENSE.md alongside), importing cn from components/pace/cn. The kit's own button/input were deleted. Result: the app's core interactive controls are consumer-owned wrappers, not receipted Pace files.
expected: If kit components are meant to be replaceable, document the consumer-owned-wrapper pattern and keep cn/provenance consistent; otherwise make the kit button/input good enough to keep.

observation: Toasts use the sonner package directly (imported in main.tsx and feature code). The kit toast component was removed with the other pruned files, so the Pace toast variant was never exercised.
expected: Either kit toast is kept and used, or docs state sonner is the supported consumer integration.

observation: dialog.tsx survives in components/pace but has zero imports in frontend/src — installed, unreceipted-drift-free, and entirely untested in this product.
expected: Installed components are either exercised or pruned; coverage claims exclude them.

observation: After the custom palette landed, a series of repair commits was needed for state contrast and affordances: 95aa941 'restore destructive contrast', 0b42954 'preserve readable primary actions at rest and on hover', 3c69f67 'give native disclosures a usable hit area', plus keyboard-focus fixes 1ef839c/98352ec. Rebinding tokens to a non-default palette did not carry readable hover/active/destructive states for free.
expected: Verify or docs name the token pairs whose contrast must be preserved under a custom brand palette; ideally a contrast gate in `pace verify`.

observation: Final shipped theme is dramatically off-brand from Pace defaults (graphite/paper/solar editorial dashboard) while kit components kept working structurally — cards, selects, textareas, skeletons survived a palette+layout restyle without component edits. Good signal for adaptability of structure; the cost was borne by app CSS.
expected: Same — components should survive aggressive re-theming.
